'''Ursula Rita Bassler''' (born 1965) is a French-German particle physicist. Bassler was the President of the [[List of presidents of the CERN Council|CERN Council]] from 2019 to 2021,<ref>{{Cite web |title=Presidents and vice-Presidents of Council {{!}} CERN Council |url=https://council.web.cern.ch/en/content/presidents-and-vice-presidents-council |access-date=2022-10-10 |website=council.web.cern.ch}}</ref> and deputy director of [[Institut national de physique nucléaire et de physique des particules|National Institute of Nuclear and Particle Physics]] (IN2P3), [[Centre national de la recherche scientifique|CNRS]], from 2014 to 2015. From 2026 on, she serves as CERN's Director for Stakeholder Relations.

== Early life and education ==
Bassler was born in [[Germany]] in 1965. She moved to [[France]] as an [[Au pair|au-pair]].<ref>{{Cite web|title=The Unifying Factor|url=https://www.helmholtz.de/en/matter/the-unifying-factor/|access-date=2020-06-17|website=www.helmholtz.de|date=27 January 2020 |language=en}}</ref> She completed her [[Doctor of Philosophy|PhD]] in [[particle physics]]  at the [[Pierre and Marie Curie University]] in 1993.<ref name=":0">{{Cite web|last=|first=|date=|title=Ursula Bassler elected as next President of the CERN Council {{!}} CERN|url=https://home.cern/news/press-release/cern/dr-ursula-bassler-elected-next-president-cern-council|archive-url=|archive-date=|access-date=2018-10-08|website=home.cern|language=en}}</ref>

== Research and career ==
She joined the [[:fr:Laboratoire de physique nucléaire et de hautes énergies|Nuclear and High Energy Laboratory]] (LPNHE), a joint research unit between the [[Centre national de la recherche scientifique]] (CNRS) and [[Pierre and Marie Curie University]], where she worked on [[collider|collider-based particle physics]].<ref name=":1" /> Bassler used data from the [[HERA (particle accelerator)|HERA particle accelerator]], where she worked on the structure of the [[proton]] as a member of the [[H1 (particle detector)|H1 experiment]] at [[DESY]] in Germany.<ref name=":0" /><ref>{{Cite journal|date=1995-07-01|title=On the kinematic reconstruction of deep inelastic scattering at HERA|journal=Nuclear Instruments and Methods in Physics Research Section A: Accelerators, Spectrometers, Detectors and Associated Equipment|language=en|volume=361|issue=1–2|pages=197–208|doi=10.1016/0168-9002(95)00173-5|issn=0168-9002|arxiv=hep-ex/9412004|last1=Bassler|first1=Ursula|last2=Bernardi|first2=Gregorio|bibcode=1995NIMPA.361..197B|s2cid=15794415 }}</ref>

In 1998 Bassler joined the [[D0 experiment|DØ experiment]] at [[Fermilab]],<ref name=":0" /><ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www-d0.fnal.gov/atwork/EndOfRun/mpc/2011-09-30_D0_End_of_Run_Party/Photo_Memories_of_DZero_Archive/From%20Alan%20Stone/people.html|title=Photographs of D0 Collaborators|last=Stone|first=Alan|website=www-d0.fnal.gov|access-date=2018-10-08}}</ref> where her responsibility was to run the online [[Calorimeter (particle physics)|calorimeter]] calibration.<ref>{{Cite web|title=DØ France Home Page|url=http://d0-france.in2p3.fr/index9c7b.html?arg=calorimetry|access-date=2020-06-17|website=d0-france.in2p3.fr}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|url=http://d0-france.in2p3.fr/WORKING_GROUPS/CALORIMETRY/CALO_CAL_OFF/calo_cal_off.html|title=The D0-France group homepage|website=d0-france.in2p3.fr|access-date=2018-10-08}}</ref> She was part of a working group on structure function providing input to the Deep Inelastic Scattering Workshop in 1999.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://cerncourier.com/deep-import-of-deep-inelastic-scattering/|title=Deep import of deep inelastic scattering – CERN Courier|website=cerncourier.com|language=en-GB|access-date=2018-10-08|date=1999-11-02}}</ref>

During the [[World Year of Physics 2005|World Year of Physics]] in 2005, Bassler kept a blog at ''Quantum Diaries''.<ref>{{Cite web|title=Quantum diaries|url=http://qd.typepad.com/20/2005/01/year_of_physics.html|access-date=2018-10-08|website=Ursula Bassler : Year of physics}}</ref> In 2006, she created the project ''Collisions'', a multi-media project with {{ill|Anaïs Prosaïc|fr}} as director, which featured the physicists and engineers who work for the [[Large Hadron Collider]]. Bassler and Prosaïc made the documentary ''Collisions'' in 2008.<ref>{{cite web|last=Bassler|first=Ursula|date=2008|title=Collisions, LHC 2008|url=http://www.archive.pariscience.fr/fr/showing/206/collisions/|access-date=|website=Videotheque CNRS|publisher=CNRS|quote=}}</ref>

In 2007 she was made Head of the Particle Physics division at the [[:fr:Institut de recherche sur les lois fondamentales de l'univers|Institute of Research of the Fundamental Laws of the Universe]] at the [[French Alternative Energies and Atomic Energy Commission]] (CEA).<ref name=":0" /><ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.franceculture.fr/personne-ursula-bassler.html#biography|title=Ursula Bassler : biographie, actualités et émissions France Culture|website=France Culture|language=fr-FR|access-date=2018-10-08}}</ref>

She was scientific deputy director in particle physics and computing at [[Institut national de physique nucléaire et de physique des particules|IN2P3]] (2014-2015), before becoming its deputy director (2016-2018).<ref name=":1">{{Cite web|last=|first=|date=|title=Annuaire de l'IN2P3 - Ursula Bassler - Direction|url=https://annuaire.in2p3.fr/agents/Y249QmFzc2xlciBVcnN1bGEsb3U9cGVvcGxlLGRjPWluMnAzLGRjPWZy/show|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20181009013310/https://annuaire.in2p3.fr/agents/Y249QmFzc2xlciBVcnN1bGEsb3U9cGVvcGxlLGRjPWluMnAzLGRjPWZy/show|archive-date=2018-10-09|access-date=2020-06-17|website=annuaire.in2p3.fr|url-status=dead}}</ref>  At [[IN2P3]], Bassler prepared the approval of the upgrades for the [[High Luminosity Large Hadron Collider|high-luminosity LHC]] (HL-LHC) detectors and the French participation in the [[European Open Science Cloud]].<ref name=":0" />

She has been member of the [[DESY]] scientific council.<ref name=":0" />

In September 2018 Bassler was made the 23rd President of [[CERN]] Council. Her candidacy was proposed by France and Germany.<ref name=":2">{{Cite web|title=DPB - September 28, 2018|url=https://franceintheus.org/IMG/html/briefing/2018/DDB-2018-09-28.html|access-date=2018-10-08|website=franceintheus.org}}</ref>

As of August 2024, Bassler is affiliated with Laboratoire Leprince-Ringuet at [[École polytechnique|École Polytechnique]] as CNRS researcher.

In June 2025, the CERN Council elected her as Director of Stakeholder Relations, following the nomination by then-Director-General Designate, [[Mark Thomson (physicist)|Mark Thomson]].<ref>{{cite web |last1=Thomson |first1=Mark |title=CERN management structure for 2026–2030, part 2 |url=https://home.cern/news/opinion/cern/cern-management-structure-2026-2030-part-2 |website=CERN |access-date=21 June 2025}}</ref>

Bassler has published more than 500 peer reviewed papers<ref>{{cite web |url=https://inspirehep.net/author/profile/U.Bassler.1 |title=Publication list for U. Bassler |website=[[INSPIRE-HEP]] |publisher=Inspire |access-date=12 Nov 2019 |archive-date=21 December 2019 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20191221184139/https://inspirehep.net/author/profile/U.Bassler.1 |url-status=dead }}</ref> and she is editor of the popular science book ''Étonnants infinis''.<ref>{{Cite book |title=Étonnants infinis |publisher=CNRS éditions |isbn=9782271143808 |editor-last=Bassler |editor-first=Ursula |publication-place=Paris |publication-date=2022 |language=FR}}</ref>
